```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "The deciding test is a paying customer within 90 days. B has direct evidence that this customer pays: Expatfile (165k+ users) and MyExpatTaxes (100k returns) charge $119–$199 per return, and incumbents charge more for the investor/PFIC tier B targets. A has direct evidence against payment: every named competitor is free or donation-supported, and the brief concedes any price is 'a bet against the market's current norm.'",
    "A's strongest precedent works against it. Fakespot, a well-funded and well-distributed product in the same category, shut down in July 2025 rather than sustain itself, which the brief reads as a sign the category struggles to monetize even at scale.",
    "B's demand evidence ties the pain to money: five-figure remediation costs, costly filing expenses and people considering renunciation. A's demand quotes are general frustration, mostly from threads where builders launched their own tools, plus a hostile counter-signal ('downright immoral'). None of A's quotes shows willingness to pay.",
    "B's main blocker is IRS e-file (EFIN) approval, which can take up to 45 days. That fits inside a 90-day window, though it strains the brief's six-week build plan. B's open question also points to a narrower PFIC-calculation wedge that could make a first sale possible without full e-filing.",
    "A's advantages are a fast, cheap build and free distribution. These help it ship, but they do not answer whether anyone pays, and it would have to displace several free alternatives already on the same store listings."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "A's price hypothesis of ~$3–5/month. Its sources are GPTZero's AI-detection tier, a different product priced higher, cited through a third-party aggregator, and 'typical consumer extension subscriptions (~$4.99/month),' which has no source and so counts as missing. Nothing in the brief shows any user of a Reddit or fake-review filter paying at any price.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. B's evidence has real gaps: pricing for Atamatax and Top Tax was not found, there is no cost data for the community channels it relies on, the 'likely higher' niche CPC is speculation, and it cites an 'open_questions' field that does not exist in the brief. B also carries trust and high-stakes execution risk that a solo newcomer may struggle to overcome. Still, B shows proven payment in its segment, while A shows proven non-payment across its category, so the gap on this question is meaningful."
}
```
